in_hebrew.name: יִנָּחָה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: A name derived from the Hebrew verb נָחַה (nachah), meaning 'to comfort, console, or delight'. In the context of a name, it signifies 'one who brings joy' or 'one who is joyful'. In the biblical context, it could be interpreted as a name of praise or thanksgiving.

in_greek.name: Οἰκονόμης
in_greek.long_meaning: In ancient Greece, the name Οἰκονόμης (Oikonomēs) was given to individuals who managed households or estates. The name is derived from the Greek words οἶκος (oikos), meaning 'house', and νόμος (nomos), meaning 'law' or 'custom'. Thus, Oikonomēs can be interpreted as 'one who manages the household' or 'one who follows the custom of the household'. In the biblical context, it could be interpreted as a name of responsibility or stewardship.

in_latin.name: Victorianus
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name Victorianus is derived from the Latin word victor, meaning 'conqueror' or 'victor'. In the biblical context, it could be interpreted as a name of victory or triumph, signifying one who has overcome adversity or defeated an enemy.
